correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 the four closed-neighborhood inequalities L>=1, R>=1, L+beta>=1, R+alpha>=1 are logically equivalent to signed domination: ordinary clique vertices give the first two, bridge vertices the latter two. For even n parity forces L,R>=2 and extra constraints are vacuous; independent binomial choices give W=P_n^2 and gamma_s=4. For odd n=2q+1 condition on both endpoint labels, giving disjoint A^2+2BC+D^2 enumerators. Minimum odd weight 2 requires both clique sums 1 and both bridge labels +1; multiplicity C(2q,q)^2. Independently enumerated ALL 2^(2n) signings and weight coefficients for each n=2..8 (total 87376) and confirmed both formulas, but unrestricted proof is symbolic.
residual_risks: Scope only equal-size K_n barbells with exactly one bridge and signed closed neighborhoods; family-specific unindexed signed-domination publication could predate this theorem. Known results on ordinary domination polynomials do not settle it.
